restoration_note: The teaching describes the Lord as Divine Human descending into the soul's members via the head/body correspondence: the First Man is the head, his five sons (mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection) are sent forth as members hanging from him, and his head rests on the Pillar of Glory in the Height. Most small gaps are well-constrained: morphological completions (ⲏ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄, ⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ, ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ), standard titles (Virgin of Light, Pillar of Glory, First Man), and parallel formulas (ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲉϥⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲉϥⲙⲟⲣⲫⲏ, ⲡⲥⲏⲩ ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ, ⲁϩϯ ⲛⲉϥ). Larger lacunae in lines 11–13, 33–35, 41–48 (the closing scene of fashioning and gathering) lack adequate constraints — only fragmentary partials and broad context — and are marked low or unrestorable to preserve honesty. The gift sequence (peace/kiss, fragrance, gathering inward) is structurally clear but the specific subjects and verbs of each line cannot be securely restored.
